instagram.author: alicialyttle
instagram.body:
Save this, then go rewrite the last prompt you sent.

Most people ask AI for a $5 answer without realizing it. “Write me a marketing email.” “Give me some content ideas.” The output isn’t bad, it’s just the tier you asked for.

The fix is one sentence. Tell it what the work is worth. “Write me the marketing email a $50,000 consultant would hand a client.” Same request, completely different standard.

Because AI doesn’t set the bar. You do. 💰🤖

Comment “SUMMIT” if you want more ways to get real work out of AI 🎉
AI knows the difference between a $5 job and a $50,000 job. AI has been trained on data, right? It and the data it's been trained on, it knows what a $5 job looks like for a marketing email and what a $50,000 job looks like to write a marketing email from a top-level consultant at a firm like McKinsey, right? That a whole group of people might write it might use it. So when you ask AI, it defaults to giving you what everybody else will get. Right? But since we're not everybody else, we're setting our standard up here. You need to tell AI what the value of the output needs to be as you assign it the job. Yes? Say money money. Right? You pay ChatGPT $20 a month. Get the most you can out of it. You're like, ChatGPT, I pay you $20 a month. You're going to write this marketing email like I paid you $50,000 and you're not going to stop until I get the best thing on the planet, right? So expect more out of your AI tools. You're just telling them to do something for you, but you're not setting the standard. You're not asking for premium, but it's about time that you did.

Add a privacy policy, add terms of service, add a refund policy, add a cookie policy. Add a cookie consent banner. Check your form consents. Don't collect unnecessary data. Audit your third party SC cases. Remove dark patterns, remove hidden fees, remove fake reviews, remove unsupported claims. Add accessibility alt text. Fix your color contrast ratio. Add keyboard navigation. Add your business details. Get age consent. If you collect kids data, add an unsubscribe link to your emails. License any fonts and images to use. Add a data deletion request option.
